A. HCN (Hydrogen Cyanide):
In HCN, the structure is H-C≡N. The carbon atom forms a single bond with hydrogen and a triple bond with nitrogen. For a carbon atom to form a triple bond, it must be sp-hybridized. This gives the carbon atom a linear geometry with bond angles of 180°.

B. HCO₂H (Formic Acid):
The structure of formic acid is H-C(=O)-OH. The carbon atom forms single bonds with hydrogen and hydroxyl group, and a double bond with oxygen. This requires sp² hybridization for the carbon atom.

C. HNO₂ (Nitrous Acid):
The structure is H-O-N=O. The nitrogen atom forms a single bond with hydroxyl group and a double bond with oxygen. This requires sp² hybridization for the nitrogen atom.

D. HNO₃ (Nitric Acid):
The structure is H-O-N(=O)=O. The nitrogen atom forms a single bond with hydroxyl group and two double bonds with oxygen atoms. This requires sp² hybridization for the nitrogen atom.

Based on this analysis, only HCN has an sp-hybridized atom (the carbon atom). The carbon in HCN forms a triple bond with nitrogen, which requires sp hybridization to create the linear geometry.
